prompt: An aircraft flies through the air with an airspeed of 120 km h^-1 directed due north. A steady horizontal wind blows from the west towards the east at 50 km h^-1. What is the ground speed of the aircraft and its track direction (bearing)?
options: Ground speed 130 km h^-1 at bearing 023 degrees
Ground speed 130 km h^-1 at bearing 067 degrees
Ground speed 170 km h^-1 at bearing 023 degrees
Ground speed 110 km h^-1 at bearing 337 degrees

answer.explanation: The velocity vectors are perpendicular: v_north = 120 km h^-1, v_east = 50 km h^-1. Resultant speed = sqrt(120^2 + 50^2) = sqrt(14400 + 2500) = sqrt(16900) = 130 km h^-1. The angle east of north is theta = arctan(50 / 120) = arctan(0.4167) = 22.6 degrees, corresponding to a standard three-figure bearing of 023 degrees.

distractor_explanations: Correct. Speed = sqrt(120^2 + 50^2) = 130 km h^-1; angle east of north = arctan(50/120) = 22.6 degrees -> bearing 023 degrees.
Incorrect. Computes the complementary angle from east: arctan(120/50) = 67.4 degrees -> bearing 067 degrees.
Incorrect. Adds speeds directly as scalars: 120 + 50 = 170 km h^-1.
hints: The aircraft moves north while the wind pushes it east.
Use Pythagoras for magnitude and tangent for angle from north.
solution: Resultant speed = sqrt(120^2 + 50^2) = 130 km h^-1. Angle from north: tan(theta) = 50 / 120 = 0.4167, so theta = 22.6 degrees east of north (bearing 023 degrees). Option 1 is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Set up perpendicular vectors: 120 km h^-1 north and 50 km h^-1 east.
Step 2: Magnitude: R = sqrt(120^2 + 50^2) = 130 km h^-1.
Step 3: Direction: theta = arctan(v_east / v_north) = arctan(50 / 120) = 22.6 degrees.
Step 4: Three-figure bearing measured clockwise from North is 023 degrees. Select option 1.
